source.filename: 2024-Piston-like particle jamming for enhanced stiffness adjustment of soft robotic arm.pdf

actuation: tendon-driven (differential super-elastic NiTi wires driven by digital servos via gear and rack mechanisms)
motor and ball screw mechanism (driving a piston-like jamming rod)
constitutive_assumptions: Constant curvature bending of the arm in the bending plane
Incompressible rigid particles with constant particle volume during packing transitions from RLP to HCP and during radial expansion
Axially inextensible polyester braided tube chambers
Locally reversible compression and tension around a given jamming force, yielding equal compression and tension elastic moduli (Ec = Et) and equal area separation (alpha = pi) on the cross section
Arm central axis length remains constant during bending
Structural collapse occurs when the maximum bending stress at the proximal end equals/counteracts the axial jamming stress sbmax
Tendon sliding is smooth and all jamming units compress uniformly in the steady state
control_variables: Total arm length (~180 mm) and diameter (40 mm)
Jamming chamber segment dimensions (~26 mm diameter, 37 mm height)
Helical twist angle of braided tubes (60 degrees, alternating direction between adjacent units)
Particle material and diameter (rigid plastic particles, 1.4 mm diameter)
Tendon material and diameter (super-elastic nickel-titanium alloy wires, 1.2 mm diameter)
dependent_variables: Stiffening ratio (gamma = Delta Y_0 / Delta Y)

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: A motor and ball screw mechanism drives a piston rod to exert axial compressive jamming force on a multi-unit particle core, eliminating vacuum-pressure limits and shortening the arm flexible length.
Alternating 60-degree helical pre-twisting of adjacent braided tube chambers prevents irregular buckling and ensures uniform, stable axial compression under piston actuation.

Kinematic and Euler-Bernoulli beam models determine the piston-induced tip displacement and the maximum critical bending torque before structural collapse as a function of jamming force and bending angle.
Under a 150 N jamming force, vertical tip deflection remains minimal for tip loads up to 0.3 kg, maintaining structural integrity below the collapsing point.
The robotic arm achieves an experimental stiffening ratio between 6 and 25 under 150 N jamming force across spatial bending configurations with tip loads ranging from 0.2 kg to 0.5 kg.

Sideward bending subjects the proximal jamming unit to torsion, which yields lower stiffness than pure bending, yet particle jamming substantially enhances torsional resistance compared to the unjammed state.

The piston-driven particle jamming system achieves a maximum stiffening ratio exceeding 25, outperforming vacuum-powered particle jamming (3.35) and hybrid jamming (5.5-7) reported in recent literature.

experimental_setup: Tendon-driven continuum arm prototype (~180 mm length, 40 mm diameter) connected to a 140 mm diameter base plate
Two pairs of differential 1.2 mm super-elastic NiTi tendons sliding through spacer cover disks, driven by digital servos via differential gear and rack mechanisms for 2-DOF spatial bending

Four-unit particle jamming core with 3D-printed resin cover disks, nonelastic polyester braided tubes (26 mm diameter, 37 mm height, 60-degree alternating twists), filled with 1.4 mm rigid plastic particles at ~85% filling ratio
Linear jamming actuation via motor and ball screw driving a central piston rod through the base plate, equipped with a force sensor at the piston base to measure jamming force up to 150 N

Tip loading apparatus consisting of calibrated hooked weights (0 to 0.5 kg) hung at the arm tip to evaluate deflection across three bending configurations: (theta, c) = (0, 0), (pi/3, pi/2), and (pi/3, pi)
future_work: Combining the variable-stiffness arm with other devices, such as soft end-effectors, to conduct deeper research on grasping or manipulating
independent_variables: Added tip load mass (0 to 0.5 kg)
Spatial bending angles (theta, c), specifically (0, 0), (pi/3, pi/2), and (pi/3, pi)
limitations_inferred: Testing was limited to static loads up to 0.5 kg and jamming forces up to 150 N on a single prototype scale, leaving dynamic loading and fatigue uncharacterized
Long-term wear, friction, or degradation of the braided fabric sheath and plastic particles under cyclic piston compaction was not assessed

The analytical beam model relies on idealized assumptions of uniform curvature and equal tension/compression moduli, which may deviate under complex combined multi-axis loading and non-uniform particle compaction
Control was open-loop without real-time shape or stiffness sensing feedback during operation
limitations_stated_by_authors: When the arm bends sideward/horizontally, proximal units experience torsion, and torsional stiffness is generally lower than bending stiffness, reducing the stiffening effect
Stiffness drops rapidly once the applied load exceeds the collapsing point due to particle interlock failure
Axial piston displacement DL introduces an inflexible rigid segment at the proximal end and slightly alters the arm tip position
Excessive chamber pre-twisting damages the initial structure of the braided chamber, necessitating an experimentally tuned moderate angle (60 degrees)
Maximum initial filling ratio is constrained by the required asymmetrical elongation of chambers during bending to prevent volume/stiffness alterations
main_results: Piston-driven compaction generates jamming forces up to 150 N, eliminating the atmospheric pressure saturation inherent to vacuum-based jamming systems
The arm exhibits minimal tip deflection under 150 N jamming force for loads up to 0.3 kg, verifying that the core remains below the collapsing threshold

Stiffening ratio scales positively with jamming force and is inversely related to added load, achieving ratios between 6 and 25 under 150 N jamming force across all tested bending angles with 0.2 to 0.5 kg loads
In the unbent configuration under 150 N jamming force, the stiffening ratio is at least 15 for loads up to 0.5 kg and exceeds 25 at 0.3 kg load
Downward bending exhibits higher baseline stiffness than the unbent configuration, and particle jamming significantly enhances torsional stiffness during horizontal bending
modeling_methods: Constant curvature kinematic geometry model mapping tendon length differentials to arm bending angles (theta, c) and accounting for piston stroke inflexibility DL
Particle packing state transition formulation modeling conservation of macroscopic particle volume from random loose packing (RLP) to hexagonal close packing (HCP) with radial chamber expansion
Geometric chamber elongation constraint formulation determining the maximum permissible initial filling ratio omega

Euler-Bernoulli beam mechanics model incorporating bilinear elastic modulus formulation with equal tension-compression division (alpha = pi) to derive maximum proximal bending torque and critical collapsing load threshold M_0
performance_metrics: General bending stiffness K = Mg / DY (N/mm)
possible_gap_implications: While piston-driven jamming eliminates bulky vacuum hardware and surpasses atmospheric limits, the linear piston mechanism introduces a rigid proximal length and added mechanical complexity, pointing to an ongoing trade-off between slender continuum dexterity and high-force mechanical jamming systems

Demonstrating high-force particle jamming via motorized linear screws suggests viability for high-payload surgical or industrial continuum robots, though adapting this mechanism for multi-segment arms with independent segmental stiffness control remains an open research challenge
paper.research_objective: To develop a compact, modular piston-like particle jamming mechanism for a tendon-driven soft robotic arm that provides enhanced jamming force and superior variable stiffness adjustment exceeding conventional vacuum-driven limitations.
paper.research_problem: Soft robotic arms possess low inherent stiffness that restricts their capacity to exert large forces or carry heavy payloads, while integrating powerful stiffness-adjusting systems into space-confined slender arms remains difficult because conventional vacuum jamming is limited by atmospheric pressure and fluidic actuators consume excessive radial space.
paper.title: Piston-like particle jamming for enhanced stiffness adjustment of soft robotic arm
